definition: Divergent evolution is the development of different lines from a common ancestry. In this source, it is described as depending on isolation, meaning a population is split into separate groups so they no longer interbreed and can change in different directions.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Isolation; pinned source text

reasons: The definition claims divergent evolution is “development of different lines from a common ancestry,” but the provided packet does not mention common ancestry in relation to divergent evolution (it discusses isolation and “polytypic (or divergent) evolution”).

The definition’s claim that divergent evolution “depends on isolation” is only indirectly supported: the packet says Gulick and Romanes contend that “all polytypic (or divergent) evolution involves isolation,” but the packet does not itself define divergent evolution as a general process conditioned by isolation in those exact terms.

The packet’s content is anchored to “Isolation” and discusses isolation mechanisms (including geographical isolation and sterility barriers), not a standalone definition of the term “divergent evolution” as such; the supplied definition therefore extends beyond what is explicitly stated.
